title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Scammers deployed AI-generated deepfake videos and impersonation to defraud vulnerable immigrants seeking legal services. Hundreds of fraudulent social media profiles used the identity of an established immigration attorney to offer services he never provided, with promises to obtain US residency for undocumented immigrants in exchange for thousands of dollars. The impersonation operated across multiple platforms with minimal friction, reaching victims through social media and then funneling them to payment apps like Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App where the fraud could proceed without verification.

The deployment failure was the absence of identity verification on social platforms. The scammers succeeded because they could create thousands of accounts bearing a real attorney's name and likeness, receive client inquiries, and collect payment through intermediaries with no platform check that the profiles matched the actual person. Catching this would have required social media platforms to verify professional identities before allowing service-related accounts, or to flag and remove duplicative profiles at scale automatically.

It is not established whether the scammers used generative video AI to create the deepfakes or simply repurposed existing footage, nor whether the supposed testimonials from former clients were AI-generated or recorded from real people.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of artificial intelligence scammers who are using deepfake videos and fake social media profiles to defraud vulnerable immigrants. The criminals have created hundreds of fraudulent accounts depicting Leal offering immigration services he never provided, such as obtaining US residency for undocumented immigrants without deportation orders in exchange for $2,200. The scam has escalated dramatically over the past three months, with an anti-piracy company helping remove nearly 6,500 fake profiles across social media platforms, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram.

The scammers typically lure victims through social media videos that direct them to contact a WhatsApp number, where they send phony contracts and request payment through apps like Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Some fake videos feature testimonials from supposed former clients praising Leal's services. Leal has changed his personal phone number and is urging immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online while being cautious of requests for immediate payment. He plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the fraud's origins.
